compiled_state.description:
## Problem
`origin/main` is currently RED on the CI **Module-size gate**: `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` is **803 LOC**, exceeding the absolute 800-LOC hard cap (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`). The gate (`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml`, step "Module-size gate") runs `find src/rebar -name '*.py' | xargs wc -l` over the WHOLE tree with no allowlist, so this reddens EVERY open Gerrit change with `Verified -1` — no change (1377/e34a, 1379/bdb8, and any future) can reach `Verified +1` until the file is back under the cap.

Evidence:
- `git show origin/main:src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py | wc -l` -> 803 (cap 800; only file over cap on origin/main).
- Change 1377 (story e34a) got `Verified -1` solely on this gate; the file is unmodified by that change.
- The file crossed the cap around commit 339262b990 ("af11: silence unrelated ambiguity in close scan").

## Approach — split along the existing completion-precheck call-graph seam
Extract the self-contained **completion-verification precheck** cluster out of `transition_close.py` into a new sibling module `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close_precheck.py`. These four functions form a closed sub-graph — only `_completion_precheck` is called by `close_ticket`; the other three are private helpers reachable ONLY through it:
- `_completion_precheck` (the pre-close, outside-the-lock verification half; called by `close_ticket`)
- `_has_live_replacement_link` (called only by `_completion_precheck`)
- `_is_live_ticket` (called only by `_has_live_replacement_link`)
- `_referencing_commit_exists` (called only by `_completion_precheck`)

The module-level constant `_NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES` (used ONLY by `_has_live_replacement_link`) moves with the cluster. `_PLAN_REVIEW_CLOSE_TYPES`, `_raise_plan_review_close_gate_error`, and `_compact_on_close` STAY in `transition_close.py` (they are called by `close_ticket`, not by the precheck). This is a genuine call-graph seam (not a mechanical trim): the cluster is the "verify" phase of the load-bearing verify->close->sign order documented in the module docstring.

Post-split sizes: `transition_close.py` ~= 480 LOC (in the 200-500 target band); new `transition_close_precheck.py` ~= 340 LOC (in band, > 100-LOC floor). No file left over 800; no file created under 100.

### Binding design — how "behavior unchanged" is GUARANTEED (the load-bearing decision)
`transition_close.py` will `from rebar._commands.transition_close_precheck import _completion_precheck, _referencing_commit_exists` at module top. This BINDS both names as attributes of the `transition_close` module object, so:
1. `close_ticket` keeps calling the bare name `_completion_precheck(...)`. Python resolves that against `transition_close`'s module globals AT CALL TIME (dynamic lookup), so it picks up the imported binding — and, crucially, ALSO picks up any monkeypatch that rebinds `transition_close._completion_precheck` (the patch replaces the module global the function body reads). The interception behavior of the three monkeypatching tests is therefore preserved without any change to how `close_ticket` references the symbol.
2. `transition_close._completion_precheck` and `transition_close._referencing_commit_exists` remain valid module attributes, so tests that call them as `_tc._completion_precheck(...)` / import `_referencing_commit_exists from transition_close` still resolve.
Because `_completion_precheck` is genuinely used by `close_ticket`, its import is not dead (no F401). `_referencing_commit_exists` is NOT used elsewhere in `transition_close.py` after the move; rather than a re-export that ruff would flag as unused, the single test that imports it (`test_transition_close.py`) is repointed to the new module (see below). `_is_live_ticket` / `_has_live_replacement_link` / `_NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES` are private to the cluster with ZERO external references (verified via grep, incl. as monkeypatch string targets), so they move cleanly with no rewiring.

### Consumers of the moved symbols (COMPLETE enumeration — grep-verified across all of `src/` and `tests/`, including string/monkeypatch targets)
`_completion_precheck`:
- `close_ticket` (same file, ~line 638) — direct call; satisfied by the module-top import (binding design above).
- Direct module-attribute calls `_tc._completion_precheck(...)` in `tests/unit/test_llm_failure_matrix.py` (2 calls), `tests/unit/test_close_gate_step_budget_message_d59e.py`, `tests/unit/test_close_gate_bound_remedy_db1c.py`, `tests/unit/test_close_gate_bound_message_d59e.py` — satisfied by the import binding (attribute still present on `transition_close`); NO edit needed.
- Monkeypatch `transition_close._completion_precheck` in `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_close_gate_lifecycle.py:59`, `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_attested_signing.py:302` (spy wrapping `tc._completion_precheck`), `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_idea_close_bypass.py:140` — satisfied by dynamic global lookup in `close_ticket` (binding design); NO edit needed.
- Docstring-only mentions in `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_completion_gate.py`, `test_close_gate_subtree.py`, `test_attested_signing.py`, `test_close_ref_target_80af.py`, `test_idea_close_bypass.py` — no code change; NO edit needed.

`_referencing_commit_exists`:
- `tests/unit/test_transition_close.py` imports it (line 24) and calls it directly (no monkeypatch of the transition_close copy) — REPOINT the import + the docstring path (line 4) to `transition_close_precheck`. Import-path-only change; assertions unchanged.

`_is_live_ticket`, `_has_live_replacement_link`, `_NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES`: no references anywhere outside the cluster (grep-verified) — move with zero rewiring.

No other `src/` module imports any of the four moved symbols (grep-verified: cross-module imports from `transition_close` are only `close_ticket`, `sign_completion_verdict`, `_verdict_manifest`, `_material_drifted` — none of which move).

## Test strategy (held-out, behavior-preserving)
This is a pure move (no logic change); the guard is the existing suite plus a new seam test:
1. Add a new test `tests/unit/test_transition_close_precheck_seam.py` (held-out; write FIRST, expect RED = ImportError before the module exists): asserts `transition_close_precheck` exposes `_completion_precheck` and `_referencing_commit_exists`; asserts `transition_close._completion_precheck is transition_close_precheck._completion_precheck` (the binding); and asserts that monkeypatching `transition_close._completion_precheck` is observed by `close_ticket` (drive a minimal close and confirm the patched sentinel ran) — locking in the binding contract that makes the move safe.
2. Repoint `tests/unit/test_transition_close.py`'s import of `_referencing_commit_exists` to the new module; its existing assertions must stay green unchanged.
3. Run the full close/completion suites with NO assertion edits and confirm green: `tests/unit/test_llm_failure_matrix.py`, `tests/unit/test_close_gate_step_budget_message_d59e.py`, `tests/unit/test_close_gate_bound_remedy_db1c.py`, `tests/unit/test_close_gate_bound_message_d59e.py`, `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_close_gate_lifecycle.py`, `test_attested_signing.py`, `test_idea_close_bypass.py`, `test_completion_gate.py`, `test_close_gate_subtree.py`, `tests/unit/test_attestation_signing.py`, `tests/unit/test_llm_disposition_plumbing.py` — proving the monkeypatch/direct-call consumers still work.
4. `make lint` + `make typecheck` clean; module-size contract test (`tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py`) green.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` is <= 800 LOC (target 200-500), split ONLY along the completion-precheck call-graph seam above — not a mechanical trim, and no new file < 100 LOC.
- [ ] New module `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close_precheck.py` holds the four precheck functions + `_NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES`, within the 100-800 LOC policy band.
- [ ] `transition_close.py` imports `_completion_precheck` (and re-binds it as a module attribute) so both direct module-attribute calls AND `transition_close._completion_precheck` monkeypatches in the existing tests keep steering `close_ticket` — verified by a new seam test.
- [ ] The CI Module-size gate passes (no `src/rebar/**/*.py` over 800), restoring reachable `Verified +1` on Gerrit changes.
- [ ] All listed close/completion tests pass with NO assertion changes (behavior unchanged); only `test_transition_close.py`'s import path is repointed.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` clean.
